title: Blasted Lands
body: The Blasted Lands were once the southern half of the Black Morass, a dark fen of marsh and mire. It was here that Medivh and the warlocks of the Shadow Council opened the Dark Portal, and the orcish Horde poured through into Azeroth. The energies of the gate dried and warped the land into a red and barren waste where lightning flickers without end and even the beasts have grown unnaturally strong. At the close of the Second War the broken Horde made its last stand at the foot of the portal, and afterwards the Kirin Tor raised Nethergarde Keep in the northern hills to keep watch over the gate. The demons never truly left. The dreadlord Razelikh rules the wastes through his Shadowsworn cult and the Dreadmaul ogres, and the Burning Legion's soldiers gather in the Tainted Scar.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Blasted_Lands (southern part of the Black Morass, dried and warped by the portal's magic, constant lightning, Nethergarde built by Khadgar and the Kirin Tor, Razelikh and the Shadowsworn, Legion in the Tainted Scar)

parts.body: The Dark Portal itself stands dark and silent. For twenty years no army has passed through it, and it looms over the southern wastes as a monument to wars half forgotten, watched day and night by the riftwatchers and analysts of Nethergarde.

parts.body: A new shadow has fallen over the wastes. Necropolises of the Scourge hang in the red sky above the heart of the Blasted Lands, and around the necrotic shards beneath them skeletal shocktroopers, ghoul berserkers and spectral soldiers spread across the land while the cultists who serve them labor in their shadow.

parts.body: Now the Dark Portal has woken. Demons pour through it in an endless tide, felguards, voidwalkers, infernals and dreadknights with their hounds, and at its foot the Argent Dawn fights a desperate battle beside the mages of Nethergarde and champions of the Alliance and the Horde. If the line breaks, the Argent Dawn warns, there will be no end to the demons' fire.

parts.body: Twenty years of silence ended when the Burning Legion forced demons through the Dark Portal. Nethergarde and the Argent Dawn held them at bay until the armies of Azeroth arrived and drove them back through the gate. Now the Alliance and the Horde march through the wastes and on into Outland, where a savage war rages on the far side.

npc_text 9969 (Dar'toon)

title: Nethergarde Keep
body: Nethergarde Keep stands in the northern hills of the Blasted Lands, a Dalaranian fortress raised after the Second War at the urging of Archmage Khadgar to guard against any new invasion through the Dark Portal. The Kirin Tor have manned it ever since, and its analysts and riftwatchers keep a close eye on the gate. Khadgar himself held command here until the gate was reopened and he led the Alliance into Draenor. Today the keep lives on supplies sent from Darkshire, too many of which go astray on the road, its library holds histories of the portal's wars, and an ambassador within its walls urges the Alliance to set aside its quarrel with the Horde and face the true enemy.

title: Garrison Armory
body: In the hills beside Nethergarde Keep, the Garrison Armory is the keep's working mine. Nethergarde miners, watched over by foremen and engineers, cut mithril and truesilver from the rock, and what they dig is sent to Stormwind in trade for the many supplies a fortress in the wastes cannot produce for itself. Its tunnels run deep beneath the hills. The crews guard their ore jealously, and any Horde prospector who slips inside hoping to work the veins will find the miners turning on him at once.

title: Dreadmaul Hold
body: In the northwest corner of the Blasted Lands squats Dreadmaul Hold, once an orc settlement until the Dreadmaul ogres drove the orcs out after the Second War and gave it their own name. Behind its barracks and smithy, ogres, ogre mages and brutes answer to Grol the Destroyer, who serves Razelikh the Defiler. Near his seat stands a stone of binding, where servants the Defiler granted to Grol are held in bondage. Starving snickerfang hyenas lurk at the edges of the camp, and a rarely seen ogre called Mojo the Twisted walks among the brutes.

title: Altar of Storms
body: On the western edge of the wastes stands the Altar of Storms, one of the few such altars left in Azeroth, raised here by Lady Sevine, one of the three masters of the Shadowsworn. Her followers keep it: enforcers, warlocks and dreadweavers who have given themselves over to the demon lord Razelikh. Sevine holds court beside the altar, and a stone of binding nearby holds the servants the Defiler granted to her.

title: Rise of the Defiler
body: The craggy peaks at the heart of the Blasted Lands belong to Razelikh the Defiler. His lair sits on the highest summit, reachable only by runes of teleportation, and a spirit called the Deathly Usher, bound eternally to this cursed world, waits below and asks what those who come before him desire. At the summit stands the Altar of the Defiler. Nearby, in a crater, lives Kum'isha the Collector, one of the Lost Ones, who gathers draenethyst in the hope of opening a road back to the world he lost.

title: The Serpent's Coil
body: The Serpent's Coil is a winding cave system in the eastern Blasted Lands, its mouth ringed by the burnt-out shells of orcish buildings left from the Second War. Shadowsworn cultists, thugs and adepts guard it for Archmage Allistarj, the master of this labyrinth and one of the Defiler's three chief servants. A great fel beast prowls the back cave, and a stone of binding nearby holds the servants the Defiler granted to Allistarj. Redstone basilisks hunt among the ruins.

Kirith never left. The fel beast in the back cave is what Allistarj made of him, and the servants bound to the stone nearby are souls of the same fallen regiment.

title: Dreadmaul Post
body: Dreadmaul Post is an ogre mound of the Dreadmaul clan, raised in the wastes nearer the Dark Portal, through which the ogres first came from Draenor and close to which they have stayed ever since. Dreadmaul maulers and warlocks hold it, and felbeasts prowl the ground around it. Here too stands a stone of binding where Grol keeps more of the servants the Defiler granted him. Now and then a rarely seen ogre known as Magronos the Unyielding walks among them.

title: The Dark Portal
body: The Dark Portal looms over the southern Blasted Lands, the colossal gate through which the orcish Horde first came to Azeroth. Shattered at the end of the Second War, it woke once more for a short while, when the Alliance marched through it into Draenor, and then fell silent. Felguard sentries and felhounds roam its approaches, and among them stands a stone of binding where servants of Razelikh are held.

title: The Tainted Scar
body: In the southwest of the Blasted Lands lies the Tainted Scar, where the portal's energies left the soil the color of blood. It is the Burning Legion's stronghold on this side of the gate, where felguard elites, manahounds, dreadlords and doomguard commanders gather in strength. After the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal, Lord Kazzak led its remnants here, and from the Scar he sent Razelikh to bring the wastes to heel. At an altar on the northern edge the aged warlock Daio the Decrepit lives among the demons, teaching others to bind them.

Here the host he gathered still holds the blood-red soil.

title: Razelikh the Defiler
body: Razelikh the Defiler is the dreadlord who rules the Blasted Lands. When the Legion's host was driven back into the Tainted Scar, Lord Kazzak sent him out to bring the wastes to heel, and the Shadowsworn cult and the Dreadmaul ogres now do his bidding through his three chief servants. His lair crowns the highest summit of the Rise of the Defiler, and he shows himself only when called at the altar there. Then he roars for Ilifar, Keeper of Souls, to face his challengers as his champion, and calls the flames of chaos down upon them.

parts.body: The demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes told the rest. In the age of war Razelikh was the most feared of Kazzak's lieutenants, and in the Blasted Lands he united the scattered sects of the Shadow Council with the brutish Dreadmaul. It was the ruin of Thrall's Grasp that sealed the bargain. The regiment's stolen souls became immortal servants for the three leaders, who took near-limitless power in exchange for eternal service, and the amulet he made for them, worn in three pieces, is the only key that calls him down.

title: Allistarj, Sevine and Grol
body: Three servants rule the Blasted Lands in Razelikh's name. Archmage Allistarj is master of the Serpent's Coil, where Shadowsworn cultists, thugs and adepts guard his labyrinth. Lady Sevine, a warlock of the Shadowsworn, raised the Altar of Storms on the western edge of the wastes, and her enforcers and dreadweavers keep it. Grol the Destroyer, lord of the Dreadmaul ogres, holds Dreadmaul Hold. Beside each of them stands a stone of binding that holds servants the Defiler granted them, and between them they keep the wastes for the dreadlord while he waits on his summit.

Grol killing Loramus is Cataclysm and left out. Fix: the parts conversion kept the opening on the grounds that the three cannot die without the chain's fel weapons, but the module credits a KILL to every group member in reward range, so a member without the chain who joins the kill read the amulet (2743), the deathlessness (2744), the souls of Thrall's Grasp (Swamp of Sorrows 2801) and the torture of the commander and Kirith (2721). The opening now tells only what the Place openings 403, 404 and 406 and npc_text 1454 already show; those reveals moved to parts 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 2721), 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 2743) and 3 (QUEST_DONE 2744, with Loramus' npc_text 1815). Entry triggers unchanged.

parts.body: The servants at their stones had been men of Thrall's Grasp, whose souls Razelikh tore out and shared among his lieutenants, three to each. It was Allistarj, too, who held the regiment's captured commander and his lieutenant Kirith in the Serpent's Coil and tortured them both, until Kirith's will faltered and his screams rang through the halls of the cave.
sources: quest 2721 description
npc_text 1452, 1453, 1454 (Swamp of Sorrows, shown while on 2801)

parts.body: Kirith's spirit told what makes the three so vital to their master. Each wears around the neck a third of an amulet of Razelikh's making, the very key needed to summon the demon lord, and he cannot be reached until all three have fallen.
sources: quest 2743 description
quest 3627 description (to reach the Defiler you must first destroy the triad)

parts.body: Killing them is no simple matter. In exchange for their servitude Razelikh granted each near-limitless power within the Blasted Lands, and the amulet pieces, attuned to their owners' lifeforce, keep them from death by any ordinary means as long as they remain there. Loramus Thalipedes saw the cruelty of the bargain: just as their servants were bound to the land, so were they, and the price of their immortality was imprisonment and eternal servitude under Razelikh.
sources: quest 2744 description
npc_text 1815, 1816 (Loramus gossip, shown while on quest 3141, offered on turning in 2744)

title: Kirith
body: Kirith the Damned is a great fel beast, a hulking felhound that prowls the back cave of the Serpent's Coil, deep in the labyrinth Archmage Allistarj holds for the Defiler. It burns away the magic of those who face it and tears through their armor. Yet the beast is not all it seems. When it falls, a ghostly figure rises from the body and lingers for a short while, as if death had set something free: the Spirit of Kirith. To those who have no business with it, the spirit keeps its silence.
sources: smart_scripts 7728 (Mana Burn, Pierce Armor; on death casts Spirit of Kirith)

Part 1: he became Kirith the Damned and his spirit rose (KILL 7728, QUEST_DONE 2721, TALK 7729, the spirit that appears on his death). Part 2: the summoning secret (QUEST_ACCEPT 2743, offered by the spirit). Before: verified. Spirit of Kirith 7729 is a quest NPC (npcflag 2, faction 35). The opening now holds only what such a character sees: the felhound in the back cave, its spells, the spirit rising on its death (smart_scripts 7728) and its silence (7729 has no gossip menu or greeting, only quests 2721 and 2743). The capture, torture and what he became moved into part 1 on QUEST_DONE 2721 alone (KILL 7728 and TALK 7729 dropped from it); part 2 unchanged. Entry triggers unchanged.

parts.body: Kirith had been lieutenant of Thrall's Grasp. When the regiment was overwhelmed he fell into the hands of Archmage Allistarj, and his commander, captured later, was held beside him, the two tortured in turn. Where the commander endured, Kirith's will faltered, and his screams rang through the halls of the cave as the experiments went on. What came out of them was the beast. Only in death could what remained of him speak, and his spirit was startled to learn who had sent for him: Trebor, his old commander.

parts.body: Kirith's spirit knew its time was limited and did not mince words. Grinning, it told how the Defiler's servants guard the secret of summoning their master, for the key to calling him down hangs around their own necks.
sources: quest 2743 description

title: Kum'isha the Collector
body: Kum'isha the Collector is one of the Lost Ones, a draenei exile who lives in a crater near the Rise of the Defiler, stranded far from his homeland. He has given his life to the search for flawless spheres of draenethyst, crystals so rare that draenei have died seeking a single one, for with them he believes he can open a rift back to the world he lost. To his senses every race of Azeroth gives off the same dizzying reek of greed, and since it was greed that cost him his home, he means to let greed carry him back. He pays in trinkets for any fragment brought to him, and despises those who take the payment.
sources: npc_text 1302, 1303

title: Bloodmages Drazial and Lynnore
body: Bloodmage Drazial and his sister Lynnore, elven practitioners of blood magic, keep a small camp near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands. They believe the energy unleashed when the Dark Portal opened seeped into the beasts of the region and drove them to evolve into their present forms. Drazial studies the body: hyena jowls able to snap through thorium steel, the lungs of blasted boars, the decisive strike of the scorpok. Lynnore studies mind and spirit, from the cunning of the redstone basilisk to the vigor hidden in vulture gizzards. Both distill their findings into potent assays, though Drazial's love of science never strays far from thoughts of profit.

title: Quartermaster Lungertz
body: Quartermaster Lungertz keeps Nethergarde Keep supplied, no easy task at the far end of a road that winds through Deadwind Pass and the Swamp of Sorrows. Crates of powerstones for the keep's mages must be rushed from Darkshire before their power fades, barrels stamped with his name turn up lost along the way, and whole caravans have gone astray on the swamp road. The keep's stock of Azoran crystals, a reagent its wizards need, is running low. As he reminds every visitor, Nethergarde always needs more: supplies for its mages' research and supplies to keep its defenders fit to fight.

title: Watcher Mahar Ba
body: Watcher Mahar Ba is one of the watchers of Nethergarde Keep, a scholar eager to understand the forces at work around him. Some time ago he sent a request to Master Mazen of the Academy of Arcane Arts and Sciences in Stormwind for Khadgar's Essays on Dimensional Convergence, the writings of the very archmage at whose urging the keep was built, and he still waits for them to arrive.
sources: quest 1364 description and reward text

parts.body: The essays came at last, though not as planned. The young courier carrying them lost his way in the Swamp of Sorrows and dropped them as he fled from plantlike creatures of the marsh, and a determined traveler brought them on. Mahar Ba had feared his request overlooked, Mazen being bogged down with so many strange happenings. To glimpse the insight of one as great as Khadgar excites him beyond words.
sources: quest 1364 description and reward text

title: Thadius Grimshade
body: Thadius Grimshade is a Wildhammer dwarf who left Aerie Peak years ago in pursuit of darker knowledge, and now works as a diviner in the mage tower of Nethergarde Keep. His rituals can follow the thread between an object and its owner, though he warns onlookers to make no sound, since a single misstep could spell their doom. He does nothing for free. When the gryphon master of Aerie Peak sought his help to find the lost gryphon Sharpbeak, Grimshade first demanded the medallion of the Zul'Farrak troll Nekrum, hoping to learn how it had lengthened its bearer's life without paying its unpleasant price.

title: Daio the Decrepit
body: Daio the Decrepit is an aged human warlock, once a mage, who has settled at an altar on the northern edge of the Tainted Scar among the Legion's own soldiers. There he teaches the infernal arts to younger warlocks, above all the binding of greater demons. To cage a doomguard, he teaches, one needs a crystal prison shaped from the Tears of the Hederine, an anti-magic crystal from the demons of Winterspring, bound with the blood of the Wildspawn satyrs of Dire Maul, and even then the demon will fight savagely against capture. He holds no illusions about such power: those who wield it, he says, pay grossly for it.

title: Netherwane and Dar'toon
body: At the foot of the Dark Portal two camps stand side by side. Watch Commander Relthorn Netherwane of Nethergarde remembers the battle fought here not long ago, when the keep and the Argent Dawn held back a tide of demons until the kingdoms of Azeroth came to drive them through the gate. He never thought to see the portal open again, and fears the quiet hides the madness beyond it. Warlord Dar'toon of the Horde speaks of the same battle with open envy, wishing he had been there when the demons clashed with Azeroth's heroes. Both now send every soldier they can spare through the gate to the war in Outland.

title: Through the Dark Portal
body: For twenty years the Dark Portal stood silent, a monument to wars half forgotten. The histories kept at Nethergarde tell its story. Opened by Medivh and the Shadow Council, it carried the Horde into Azeroth, and when the Horde broke at the end of the Second War its last clans fell at the foot of the gate. A few months after the keep was finished the portal woke again, and Khadgar and Turalyon led the Alliance into Draenor, then destroyed the gate from the far side to spare Azeroth. Then the Burning Legion forced it open once more. Nethergarde and the Argent Dawn held until the armies of the Alliance and the Horde drove the demons back. Now both sides call for volunteers, for beyond the gate rages a savage war their commanders fear they cannot win alone.

title: The Fall of the Defiler
body: With the souls of Thrall's Grasp set free, the regiment's fallen commander turns to the one man still unaccounted for: his lieutenant Kirith. The two were imprisoned together and tortured by Archmage Allistarj, but Kirith's will faltered, and his screams rang through the halls of the cave as the experiments went on. That was the last the commander saw or heard of him. As one chapter closes another begins, and the commander's work against the demon lord who destroyed his regiment, Razelikh the Defiler, is not yet over.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Razelikh_the_Defiler
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Fallen_Hero_of_the_Horde

parts.body: Kirith was found in the Serpent's Coil, twisted by Allistarj's experiments into a great fel beast, and only in death could what remained of him speak. His spirit was startled to learn who had sent the messenger: Trebor, his old commander, the fallen hero of the Horde.
sources: quest 2721 reward text (Trebor? Trebor sent you?)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Fallen_Hero_of_the_Horde

parts.body: Kirith did not mince words. The Defiler is shielded by a triad of power, Archmage Allistarj, Lady Sevine and Grol the Destroyer, and each wears around the neck a third of an amulet of Razelikh's making: the very key needed to summon the demon lord. The triad must be destroyed.
sources: quest 2743 description

parts.body: That would be no simple task. In exchange for their servitude Razelikh granted the three nearly unlimited power within the Blasted Lands, and the amulet pieces, attuned to their lifeforce, keep them from death as long as they remain there. For help the commander sent his champions across the sea to the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes in Azshara.
sources: quest 2744 description

parts.body: The search for a weapon led to azsharite crystals from the south of Azshara and to Galvan the Ancient of the Mithril Order in Stranglethorn, who forged fel weapons able to weaken the three. Armed at last, the champions slew the triad and joined the amulet once more, and the Defiler, sensing the break in his chain of command, knew they were coming for him.
sources: quests 3141, 3602, 3621, 3625, 3626 (descriptions and reward texts)
quest 3627 description and reward text

parts.body: They bore the amulet to the altar atop the Rise of the Defiler and called the demon lord down. Razelikh fell, and his severed horn was carried back to the commander, who hailed a day to be remembered for all eternity: the demonic overlord of the Blasted Lands had fallen, and the horn would stand as proof that heroes still exist in this war torn world.
sources: quest 3628 description and reward text

title: Kum'isha's Spheres
body: Somewhere in the Blasted Lands, Kum'isha the Collector insists, flawless spheres of draenethyst can still be found, though draenei have spent whole lifetimes searching for one and died with their purpose unfulfilled. Any creature of the wastes might carry one. He asks anyone willing, greedy as he believes them all to be, to bring him such a sphere in exchange for riches beyond their wildest dreams, for with it he hopes a rift may be opened to his homeland. Meanwhile he buys flawed fragments, which may still serve his people in other ways, paying in trinkets and scorn alike. His junk heap shrinks while theirs grows, which on Draenor, he says, counts as a fair trade.
sources: quests 2521, 2522, 3501, 3502 (descriptions and reward texts)
creature_text 7363 groups 0-4
npc_text 1302

parts.body: When a sphere at last reached him he could hardly believe his eyes. He set it hovering before him, chanted in an unknown tongue and tore open a rift, crying out to his brethren to rise and go home to Outland before it closed. Afterward, he remarked, one could see why he lives in a crater.

parts.body: Yet Kum'isha counts the conjuration a failure. The hope of the draenei, he says, is as fervent as any greed for trinkets, and he remains hopeful that his next attempt will succeed. He sends the greedy back out into the cursed lands to find him another sphere.
sources: quest 2522 description
